title: Fitting bias binding to a box cushion edge
subtitle: Cut true-bias strips, join them into a continuous length, and stitch the binding over the top and bottom seam lines of a box cushion
excerpt: How to apply bias binding to the seam edges of a box cushion. Covers cutting fabric on the true bias, joining strips by diagonal seam, folding and pressing the binding, stitching to the top panel seam, folding over, and finishing the underside.
sourceNotes: Traditional upholstery and soft furnishing practice, public domain. UK trade upholstery practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A strip of fabric cut at 45 degrees to the warp and weft (the true bias) that stretches slightly in both length and width. This stretch allows it to curve around rounded and mitred corners without puckering, making it the correct choice for finishing curved seam edges, shaped cushion borders, and piping covers.

The side panel of a box cushion that connects the top panel to the bottom panel, forming the side depth of the cushion. For a 100 mm deep cushion, the boxing strip is 100 mm wide plus seam allowances. It is cut and joined to form a continuous loop around the full perimeter of the cushion.

gives a clean, flexible edge that lies flat around corners and curves. INTERMEDIATE: cutting true bias and mitring the strip joins takes care.

Fold the fabric diagonally so one selvedge runs parallel to the crossgrain. The fold line is the true bias. Cut strips along lines parallel to this fold, each strip 40 to 45 mm wide for a 15 mm finished binding. Cut enough strips to go around the full cushion perimeter twice (for top and bottom edges), plus 200 mm for joins.

Join the strips end to end by placing two strip ends right sides together at a right angle, with the join diagonal between them. Stitch across the diagonal join. Press the seam open and trim the dog-ear corners flush with the strip edges. The joins sit at a 45-degree angle so they do not show as a ridge on the finished binding.
Fold, press, and stitch the binding

Press the binding strip in half lengthwise, wrong sides together. Pin the raw edges of the binding to the raw edge of the top panel seam, right sides together, starting at a seam join on the boxing strip. Stitch through the seam allowance at 15 mm. Fold the binding over to the underside of the boxing strip and slip-stitch or machine-stitch in the ditch from the top to secure the folded edge.

At each corner, stop stitching exactly at the seam point. Fold the binding strip back at 45 degrees to form a mitre, then fold it around the corner and continue stitching along the next side. The mitre fold distributes the corner bulk evenly on both faces of the binding.

attrs.symptom: Binding puckers around the cushion corners
attrs.cause: The fabric was cut off the true bias, so it does not have the stretch needed to curve around the corner.
attrs.fix: Check the cut angle on new strips by folding the fabric diagonally until the selvedge lies on the crossgrain before marking. Puckered corners on the existing binding can be loosened and eased with a damp cloth and iron.

attrs.symptom: Binding shows a ridge at the join between strips
attrs.cause: The join between strips was made on the straight grain rather than on the diagonal.
attrs.fix: Join strips with the diagonal seam method, with the two strip ends placed at 90 degrees to each other rather than straight across.
